purpose: absdelay history is accepted-step state: the delayed ramp is exact across four rejection bursts.

oracle.derivation: The input is $abstime (LRM 9.10), so absdelay(input, td) at time t is the input at t - td (LRM 4.5.7): v(dl) = t - 0.1 for t >= 0.1. For t < 0.1 LRM 4.5.15 gives the operator no state history prior to t == 0, so the output holds the t == 0 input value, 0. Samples: 0.05 -> 0; 0.2 -> 0.1; 0.4 -> 0.3; 0.6 -> 0.5; 0.8 -> 0.7; 1.0 -> 0.9, all clear of the t = 0.1 kink. The input is linear in t, so the history interpolation is exact. N2 forces rejected-and-retried steps at t = 0.125, 0.375, 0.625, 0.875; a history sample pushed on a rejected attempt records a time that never happened (LRM 8.4.7).
